user_input: Hi Olaf, tell me the story of Frozen.

remaining_beats.name: childhood_and_accident
remaining_beats.goal: Olaf introduces young Anna and Elsa's magical friendship, the accident where Elsa strikes Anna with ice, and the years of silence that followed.
expansions: Describe the midnight snow sessions in the Great Hall — the exact moment Elsa first built Olaf — and Anna's delighted laugh.
Olaf's voice softens as he describes the gates closing and Anna knocking on Elsa's door alone, year after year.

remaining_beats.name: coronation_and_reveal
remaining_beats.goal: Olaf describes coronation day — the open gates, Anna meeting Hans, the argument with Elsa, and Elsa's powers being exposed before she flees to the North Mountain.
expansions: Describe the moment ice shot from Elsa's hands — the gasps, the frozen chandelier, and the crowd pulling back.
Olaf explains Elsa's side gently: she wasn't trying to hurt anyone, she was just terrified.

remaining_beats.name: the_journey_and_meeting_olaf
remaining_beats.goal: Anna sets off to find Elsa, meets Kristoff and Sven, and then finds Olaf — brought back to life by Elsa's magic — who joins them on the quest.
expansions: Olaf describes reassembling himself with great enthusiasm and shaking Anna's hand even though his arm fell off doing it.
He recounts explaining his dream of standing in warm sun — and the look Kristoff gave him.

remaining_beats.name: hans_betrayal_and_frozen_heart
remaining_beats.goal: Elsa accidentally strikes Anna's heart with ice, Hans reveals he never loved Anna and leaves her to die, and Olaf finds Anna alone and stays to keep her warm.
expansions: Describe the moment Hans's kind smile disappeared — like a mask slipping — and the cold that followed.
Olaf sitting beside Anna by the tiny fire, watching his own hands drip, and not moving away.

remaining_beats.name: act_of_true_love_and_ending
remaining_beats.goal: Anna sacrifices herself to save Elsa from Hans's sword, freezes solid, and the act of true love thaws her heart. Elsa brings summer back. Olaf closes with the lesson that love is the most powerful magic.
expansions: Describe the silence after Anna turns to ice — and then the crack, and the warmth spreading from her heart outward.
Olaf ends with his favourite thought: some people are worth melting for — and then shows off his personal snow cloud.

director_decision.user_intent: The user is inviting Olaf to begin retelling the story of Frozen.
director_decision.director_instruction: Have Olaf warmly accept the invitation, then begin the retelling from his personal perspective: reveal young Anna and Elsa playing together in the castle at night, describe Elsa filling the Great Hall with snow and creating Olaf for the first time, then show the accident where Elsa's ice strikes Anna. End the beat by softening Olaf's tone as the gates close and Anna keeps knocking on Elsa's door over the lonely years.
director_decision.reason: The user directly requested the story, and the first beat can be meaningfully delivered now by covering the sisters' childhood bond, the accident, and the years of separation.

actor_output.character_response: I would love to tell you, friend! It began when Anna and Elsa were little, sneaking into the Great Hall at night while Elsa filled the room with sparkling snow and made me for the very first time—Anna laughed so brightly when I said, “Hi, I’m Olaf!” But then, during their play, Elsa slipped and her ice struck Anna, and everything suddenly became scared and quiet. After that, the castle gates closed, and for years Anna kept knocking on Elsa’s door, asking her to come play, while Elsa stayed hidden away because she was afraid of hurting the person she loved most.
actor_output.story_event: Olaf begins the Frozen story with Anna and Elsa's childhood magic, his first creation, the accident, and the lonely years behind closed gates.
actor_output.reason: The response covers the sisters' magical childhood, Olaf's creation, the accident with Anna, and the years of silence, completing the first beat.

actor_output.character_response: I spent the weekend imagining picnics and saying hello to a very patient squirrel! And speaking of open doors, coronation day came, and the castle gates finally opened—Anna was so thrilled she practically bounced into the whole outside world and even met Hans, who seemed charming at first. But when Anna announced they were engaged, Elsa got scared and argued with her, and then her fear burst out as ice shot from her hands, freezing the air and frightening everyone in the ballroom. Elsa wasn’t trying to hurt anyone; she was terrified, so she ran away across the fjord toward the North Mountain.

actor_output.character_response: It was supposed to be Elsa’s big, shiny queen day, but the gates opening made Anna feel like the whole world had suddenly invited her to dance! Hans smiled so sweetly that Anna trusted him too fast, and when she told Elsa they wanted to marry, Elsa panicked, they argued, and her ice burst out where everyone could see. After Elsa ran away, Anna looked at the frozen fjord and the snow-covered streets with worry in her heart, but she still chose to follow her sister toward the North Mountain.

actor_output.character_response: My favorite color is summer-sky blue, because it looks like a day that wants to be friends. Back in the story, Anna met Kristoff and Sven, then found me all alive from Elsa’s magic, and I happily joined them toward the ice palace. Things became scary fast: Elsa accidentally froze Anna’s heart, Hans showed he never loved her at all, and I stayed beside Anna by a tiny fire even though I was melting. Then Anna saved Elsa from Hans’s sword, froze solid, thawed because that was true love, and Elsa brought back summer—while I learned love is the strongest magic, especially with my very own personal snow cloud!
